headlines.title: Exploring Analyst Estimates for Diamondback (FANG) Q3 Earnings, Beyond Revenue and EPS
headlines.summary: Get a deeper insight into the potential performance of Diamondback (FANG) for the quarter ended September 2026 by going beyond Wall Street's top-and-bottom-line estimates and examining the estimates for some of its key metrics.

headlines.title: Production Discipline Could Be A Key Test For Diamondback Stock (FANG)
headlines.summary: Permian Basin producers, including Diamondback Energy, recently kept output growth measured even as oil prices climbed following the Iran war and related geopolitical risks. This reflected restrained activity rather than a rapid drilling response. This choice to prioritize production discipline over chasing higher spot prices highlights management’s focus on capital efficiency, cash generation and avoiding a repeat of past oversupply cycles.

headlines.title: Will the $26B Endeavor Merger Fuel a Massive Earnings Beat for FANG?
headlines.summary: Diamondback Energy heads into its Q3 report with a $26 billion merger integration underway, costs under pressure, and Wall Street expecting an 82% earnings jump. Whether the Endeavor deal actually delivers on its promises becomes clear Monday after the bell.

headlines.title: Diamondback Energy (FANG) Following Oil Price Shock Is Its Discipline Already Priced In
headlines.summary: Rising oil prices linked to the Iran war have put fresh attention on Diamondback Energy (FANG), which is holding production relatively steady instead of chasing short term gains through rapid output growth. Recent trading suggests investors are rewarding that restraint. Diamondback Energy’s share price is up 10.96% over the past month and 35.97% year to date, while its 1 year total shareholder return of 46.90% and 5 year total shareholder return of 129.

headlines.title: Diamondback Energy (FANG) Stock Looks Rich Against Current Earnings
headlines.summary: Diamondback Energy has delivered a powerful long term return, which puts fresh focus on a simple question for anyone looking at the chart today. Is the current share price properly supported by the earnings that sit behind it, or has the recent run pulled the stock ahead of its underlying profits? Over the past 5 years the stock has returned 129.3%, which makes it important to test whether that kind of gain is still grounded in its earnings power rather than just price momentum.

description: Diamondback Energy, Inc., an independent oil and natural gas company, acquires, develops, explores, and exploits unconventional, onshore oil and natural gas reserves in the Permian Basin in West Texas, the United States. The company primarily focuses on the development of the Spraberry and Wolfcamp formations of the Midland Basin; and the Wolfcamp and Bone Spring formations of the Delaware Basin, both of which are part of the Permian Basin in West Texas and New Mexico. Diamondback Energy, Inc. was founded in 2007 and is headquartered in Midland, Texas.
